$comment: Descriptors this repository ships that `frictionless` refuses, and why each is still here. Read scripts/check_frictionless.py before editing: an entry closes nothing. The refusal goes on being reported and this check goes on failing until the entry is deleted, and it can be deleted only by the refusal being gone. It reddens when the refusal changes, when the declaration moves, and when the fix lands, so it cannot go stale in silence. A refusal with no entry here fails too. `frictionless_version` is held to the version installed when the check runs, because a refusal measured against one implementation and read against another reads exactly like one measured now. EMPTY on purpose: all four committed descriptors were re-emitted against the corrected constraint-routing engine (finetype b2ba501a / released as 0.6.58) and are now accepted, so there is nothing left to account for. `check_frictionless.py` treats an unaccounted refusal as a fault with or without entries here, so this list staying empty is what keeps every future refusal loud rather than a matter of remembering to add an entry.
